substances.name: Amoxicillin
substances.clinicalNote: Indication-, severity-, weight- and renal-function-specific. DRX must not reduce this to one universal 'simple infection' dose.

substances.name: Amoxicillin + clavulanic acid
substances.clinicalNote: Keep exact component ratio/formulation. The captured 7:1 formulation is not recommended below CrCl 30 mL/min because adjustment recommendations are unavailable.

substances.name: Ceftriaxone
adultExamples: CAP/COPD exacerbation/intra-abdominal infection/complicated UTI: 1–2 g IV/IM once daily
HAP/complicated SSTI/bone-joint infection: 2 g IV/IM once daily
meningitis/endocarditis/neutropenic fever: 2–4 g/day; doses >2 g/day may be divided q12h
surgical prophylaxis: 2 g single pre-operative dose
paediatricExamples: 15 days–12 years and <50 kg, CAP/HAP/intra-abdominal infection/complicated UTI: 50–80 mg/kg once daily
bacterial meningitis: 80–100 mg/kg once daily, max 4 g/day
bacterial endocarditis: 100 mg/kg once daily, max 4 g/day
acute otitis media: 50 mg/kg IM single dose; selected severe/failed cases require a separate 3-day branch
substances.clinicalNote: Neonatal/prematurity restrictions and renal ceilings remain safety-gated. Existing source candidates stay review-gated until promoted.

substances.name: Co-trimoxazole
substances.doseBasis: trimethoprim component with sulfamethoxazole component preserved
doseCandidates: Adults >18 years, standard acute infection: 160 mg TMP / 800 mg SMX PO every 12 h
Age >12 to <18 years: source tablet schedule 160 mg TMP / 800 mg SMX every 12 h; source states paediatric standard is approximately 6 mg TMP + 30 mg SMX/kg/day divided BID
PJP treatment age >12/adult: 20 mg TMP + 100 mg SMX/kg/day in two or more divided doses for 14 days
Renal: CrCl >30 standard; CrCl 15–30 uses reduced Forte schedule; CrCl <15 not recommended by this SmPC
substances.clinicalNote: Never calculate from combined tablet mass. Severe skin reactions, hyperkalaemia, haematological risk and renal function require safety review.

substances.name: Ampicillin
substances.clinicalNote: Raw 1–2 g q6h / paediatric 50 mg/kg/dose is not activated without indication-, route- and formulation-specific evidence.

substances.name: Azithromycin
substances.clinicalNote: Use existing source-backed DRX regimen branches. Do not assume a universal 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2–5 schedule across all indications/formulations.

substances.name: Metronidazole
substances.clinicalNote: No universal 500 mg q8–12h rule: route, anaerobic/protozoal indication, organ function and combination therapy must be explicit.

substances.name: Meropenem
substances.clinicalNote: Sepsis is not a single fixed-dose rule. Infection site, organism/susceptibility and renal function must be part of the regimen resolver.

substances.name: Cefuroxime
substances.clinicalNote: Oral axetil and parenteral sodium are different clinical variants. A syrup rule must bind to the exact oral product concentration before mL conversion.

substances.name: Aciclovir
doseCandidates: Adult herpes simplex treatment: 200 mg PO five times daily at about 4-hour intervals, omitting night dose, usually 5 days
Adult varicella/herpes zoster: 800 mg PO five times daily at about 4-hour intervals, omitting night dose, 7 days
substances.clinicalNote: Topical skin and ophthalmic aciclovir are separate products and must not inherit oral dosing.

substances.name: Miconazole
doseCandidates: Oropharyngeal candidosis, infants 4–24 months: 1.25 mL oral gel four times daily after meals
substances.clinicalNote: Oral gel and skin cream are separate formulations. Infant gel must be divided into small portions and not placed at the back of the throat because of choking risk.
